```{r}
#| label: fig-brinley-plot
#| fig-cap: "Brinley Plot: Reaction Time Relationships. Scatter plot showing mean RT for Hard trials (y-axis) versus Easy trials (x-axis) for each participant, colored by effort condition (blue = Low effort, crimson = High effort). Reaction times are displayed in milliseconds (ms). The dashed diagonal line (slope = 1) represents proportional slowing (equal RT increase in both conditions). The solid black regression line shows the actual relationship with 95% confidence interval (shaded ribbon), with slope > 1 indicating disproportionate slowing in Hard trials relative to Easy trials. Points above the diagonal indicate participants who slowed more in Hard relative to Easy trials. This visualization connects our DDM findings to the broader cognitive aging literature on generalized slowing [@brinley1965cognitive; @cerella1985; @salthouse1996]."
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-pos: "htbp"
#| out-width: "70%"
# Dynamic: computed from behavioral_data
if (!is.null(behavioral_data) && nrow(behavioral_data) > 0) {
  subj_col <- intersect(c("subject_id", "sub"), names(behavioral_data))[1]
  rt_col <- intersect(c("rt", "same_diff_resp_secs", "resp1RT"), names(behavioral_data))[1]
  diff_col <- intersect(c("difficulty_level", "difficulty"), names(behavioral_data))[1]
  effort_col <- intersect(c("effort_condition", "effort"), names(behavioral_data))[1]
  if (!is.null(subj_col) && !is.null(rt_col) && !is.null(diff_col) && !is.null(effort_col)) {
    brinley_data <- behavioral_data %>%
      filter(!is.na(!!sym(rt_col)), !!sym(rt_col) > 0, !!sym(rt_col) < 10,
             !is.na(!!sym(diff_col)), !is.na(!!sym(effort_col))) %>%
      group_by(!!sym(subj_col), !!sym(diff_col), !!sym(effort_col)) %>%
      summarise(mean_rt = mean(!!sym(rt_col), na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = !!sym(diff_col), values_from = mean_rt, names_prefix = "mean_rt_")
    if ("mean_rt_Easy" %in% names(brinley_data) && "mean_rt_Hard" %in% names(brinley_data)) {
      brinley_plot_data <- brinley_data %>%
        filter(!is.na(mean_rt_Easy), !is.na(mean_rt_Hard)) %>%
        mutate(
          mean_rt_Easy_ms = mean_rt_Easy * 1000,
          mean_rt_Hard_ms = mean_rt_Hard * 1000,
          effort = !!sym(effort_col)
        )
      effort_levs <- unique(brinley_plot_data$effort)
      high_eff <- effort_levs[grepl("High|40", as.character(effort_levs), ignore.case = TRUE)][1]
      low_eff  <- effort_levs[grepl("Low|5", as.character(effort_levs), ignore.case = TRUE)][1]
      if (is.na(high_eff)) high_eff <- effort_levs[1]
      if (is.na(low_eff))  low_eff <- effort_levs[length(effort_levs)]
      color_map <- setNames(c("#DC143C", "#1E90FF"), c(as.character(high_eff), as.character(low_eff)))
      fit_line <- lm(mean_rt_Hard_ms ~ mean_rt_Easy_ms, data = brinley_plot_data)
      slope <- coef(fit_line)[2]
      p_brinley <- ggplot(brinley_plot_data, aes(x = mean_rt_Easy_ms, y = mean_rt_Hard_ms)) +
        geom_point(aes(color = effort), size = 1.5, alpha = 0.7) +
        geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.5) +
        geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "black", linewidth = 0.7, alpha = 0.2) +
        scale_color_manual(values = color_map, labels = c("High Effort", "Low Effort")) +
        labs(title = "Brinley Plot: Reaction Time Relationships",
             subtitle = sprintf("Easy vs. Hard difficulty (slope = %.2f)", slope),
             x = "Mean RT: Easy Trials (ms)", y = "Mean RT: Hard Trials (ms)", color = "Effort Condition") +
        theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
        theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
              plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5, color = "gray60"),
              legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
      print(p_brinley)
    } else {
include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_brinley_plot.pdf"))
    }
  } else {
    include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_brinley_plot.pdf"))
  }
} else {
  include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_brinley_plot.pdf"))
}
```

## A3. Posterior Predictive Checks and Diagnostics {#app-ch3-ppc .unnumbered}

**Conditional Accuracy Function (CAF).** The Conditional Accuracy Function (CAF) shows how accuracy varies across RT bins, providing a diagnostic for speed–accuracy tradeoffs. @fig-caf plots empirical accuracy by RT bin for each Task × Effort × Difficulty combination. Consistent with evidence-accumulation dynamics, faster responses (lower RT bins) tend toward chance accuracy, while slower responses show higher accuracy. This pattern validates the DDM's core assumption that decisions improve with longer evidence accumulation times.

```{r}
#| label: fig-caf
#| fig-cap: "Conditional Accuracy Function (CAF). Empirical accuracy by RT bin for each Task × Effort × Difficulty combination. Shows the speed–accuracy tradeoff: faster responses (lower bins) tend toward chance accuracy, while slower responses show higher accuracy, consistent with evidence accumulation over time."
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: "85%"
# Dynamic: prefer behavioral_data (fresh on re-render), else load 04_all_caf_empirical.csv
caf_file <- file.path(proj_root, "output/publish/04_all_caf_empirical.csv")
caf_from_behav <- !is.null(behavioral_data) && nrow(behavioral_data) > 0
rt_col <- if (caf_from_behav) intersect(c("rt", "same_diff_resp_secs", "resp1RT"), names(behavioral_data))[1] else NULL
acc_col_behav <- if (caf_from_behav) intersect(c("correct", "iscorr", "accuracy", "resp_is_correct"), names(behavioral_data))[1] else NULL
task_col <- if (caf_from_behav) intersect(c("task", "Task"), names(behavioral_data))[1] else NULL
diff_col <- if (caf_from_behav) intersect(c("difficulty_level", "difficulty"), names(behavioral_data))[1] else NULL
effort_col <- if (caf_from_behav) intersect(c("effort_condition", "effort"), names(behavioral_data))[1] else NULL
caf_from_behav <- caf_from_behav && !is.null(rt_col) && !is.null(acc_col_behav) && !is.null(task_col) && !is.null(diff_col) && !is.null(effort_col)

if (caf_from_behav) {
  caf_computed <- behavioral_data %>%
    filter(!is.na(!!sym(rt_col)), !!sym(rt_col) > 0, !!sym(rt_col) < 10,
           !is.na(!!sym(acc_col_behav)), !is.na(!!sym(task_col)), !is.na(!!sym(diff_col)), !is.na(!!sym(effort_col))) %>%
    mutate(
      task = factor(!!sym(task_col)),
      effort_condition = factor(case_when(grepl("High|40", as.character(!!sym(effort_col))) ~ "High", TRUE ~ "Low"), levels = c("Low", "High")),
      difficulty_level = factor(!!sym(diff_col), levels = c("Standard", "Easy", "Hard"))
    ) %>%
    group_by(task, effort_condition, difficulty_level) %>%
    mutate(bin = cut(!!sym(rt_col), breaks = 5, labels = FALSE)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(bin)) %>%
    group_by(task, effort_condition, difficulty_level, bin) %>%
    summarise(acc_emp = mean(as.numeric(!!sym(acc_col_behav)), na.rm = TRUE), bin_rt_mid = mean(!!sym(rt_col), na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  if (nrow(caf_computed) > 0) {
    p_caf <- ggplot(caf_computed, aes(x = bin_rt_mid, y = acc_emp)) +
      geom_point(size = 1.1, color = "black") + geom_path(linewidth = 0.5, color = "black", alpha = 0.6) +
      facet_grid(task + effort_condition ~ difficulty_level) +
      labs(x = "RT bin midpoint (s)", y = "Accuracy", title = "Conditional Accuracy Function: Accuracy by RT Bin",
           subtitle = "Empirical accuracy (speed-accuracy tradeoff)") +
      scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
            plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "gray50", hjust = 0.5), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
    print(p_caf)
  } else { include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_caf.pdf")) }
} else if (file.exists(caf_file)) {
  caf_data <- read_csv(caf_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
  acc_col <- intersect(c("acc_emp", "emp_caf"), names(caf_data))[1]
  bin_col <- intersect(c("bin_rt_mid", "bin"), names(caf_data))[1]
  if (!is.null(acc_col) && !is.null(bin_col)) {
    if (acc_col == "emp_caf") caf_data <- caf_data %>% rename(acc_emp = emp_caf)
    caf_plot <- caf_data %>%
      mutate(
        task = factor(task),
        effort_condition = factor(case_when(grepl("High|40", as.character(effort_condition)) ~ "High", TRUE ~ "Low"), levels = c("Low", "High")),
        difficulty_level = factor(difficulty_level, levels = c("Standard", "Easy", "Hard")),
        bin_rt_mid = as.numeric(!!sym(bin_col))
      ) %>%
      filter(!is.na(acc_emp), is.finite(acc_emp))
    if (nrow(caf_plot) > 0) {
      p_caf <- ggplot(caf_plot, aes(x = bin_rt_mid, y = acc_emp)) +
        geom_point(size = 1.1, color = "black") + geom_path(linewidth = 0.5, color = "black", alpha = 0.6) +
        facet_grid(task + effort_condition ~ difficulty_level) +
        labs(x = "RT bin midpoint (s)", y = "Accuracy", title = "Conditional Accuracy Function: Accuracy by RT Bin",
             subtitle = "Empirical accuracy (speed-accuracy tradeoff)") +
        scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
        theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
        theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
              plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "gray50", hjust = 0.5), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
      print(p_caf)
    } else { include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_caf.pdf")) }
  } else { include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_caf.pdf")) }
} else {
  include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_caf.pdf"))
}
```

**PPC Residual Heatmaps.** PPC residual heatmaps visualize model fit across the 12 experimental cells (Task × Effort × Difficulty). Each cell is colored by two fit metrics: KS statistic (Kolmogorov–Smirnov, comparing RT distributions) and QP RMSE (quantile–probability root-mean-squared error, comparing RT quantiles). Darker red indicates poorer fit. Pre-declared thresholds were KS $<$ 0.15 (warn) and $<$ 0.20 (fail), QP RMSE $<$ 0.09 s (warn) and $<$ 0.12 s (fail). Most cells show acceptable fit (light colors), with notable misfit concentrated in Easy–VDT conditions (darker red), consistent with known fast-tail underfitting in the base Wiener DDM.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ppc-heatmaps
#| fig-cap: "PPC Residual Heatmaps. KS statistic and QP RMSE by Task × Effort × Difficulty for all models (top panel) and primary model only (bottom panel). Darker red indicates larger residuals (poorer fit). The primary model shows acceptable fit across most cells, with notable misfit in Easy/VDT conditions."
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: "80%"
include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_ppc_heatmaps.pdf"))
```

## A4. Sensitivity Analyses {.unnumbered}

### A4.1 Exclusion of Sub-Chance Participants {.unnumbered}

To verify that the inclusion of 12 participants who performed at or near chance ($\leq$ 55% accuracy, compared to 50% two-alternative forced-choice baseline) in some conditions did not bias our main findings, we conducted sensitivity analyses comparing the primary model (N=67) with models fit after excluding these participants (N=55).

**Method**: We refit the primary model (Model3_Difficulty) and an additive model (Model4_Additive) on the reduced dataset excluding sub-chance participants. Parameter estimates were compared using delta (sensitivity - baseline) with conservative 95% credible intervals. If the delta CI includes zero and the baseline and sensitivity CIs overlap, we conclude the parameter is robust to exclusion.

```{=latex}
\begin{landscape}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sensitivity-subchance
#| tbl-cap: "Sensitivity Analysis: Excluding Sub-Chance Participants"
#| tbl-pos: "htbp"
#| echo: false
if (!is.null(sensitivity_summary) && exists("has_sensitivity_summary") && has_sensitivity_summary) {
  # Function to clean model names (reuse from LOO table)
  clean_model_name <- function(model) {
    model <- as.character(model)
    
    # Single parameter models
    model <- ifelse(model == "v", "Difficulty → v (drift)", model)
    model <- ifelse(model == "z", "Difficulty → z (bias)", model)
    model <- ifelse(model == "a", "Difficulty → a (boundary)", model)
    
    # Two-parameter combinations
    model <- ifelse(model == "v_z", "Difficulty → v + z", model)
    model <- ifelse(model == "v_a", "Difficulty → v + a", model)
    model <- ifelse(model == "z_a", "Difficulty → z + a", model)
    
    # Three-parameter combination
    model <- ifelse(model == "v_z_a", "Difficulty → v + a + z", model)
    model <- ifelse(model == "v_a_z", "Difficulty → v + a + z", model)
    
    # Model number formats
    model <- gsub("Model3_Difficulty", "Difficulty → v (drift)", model)
    model <- gsub("Model4_Additive", "Additive (v + a + z)", model)
    model <- gsub("Model5_Interaction", "Interaction", model)
    model <- gsub("Model10_Param_v_bs", "v + a parameterized", model)
    
    # Remove common prefixes
    model <- gsub("^Difficulty_on_", "", model)
    model <- gsub("^difficulty_", "", model)
    
    # Format underscores as separators
    model <- gsub("_", " ", model)
    
    return(model)
  }
  
  # Function to clean parameter names (reuse from DDM parameter function)
  clean_ddm_parameter <- function(param) {
    param <- as.character(param)
    original <- param
    n <- length(param)
    result <- character(n)
    
    for (i in seq_len(n)) {
      p <- param[i]
      orig <- original[i]
      
      # Determine parameter type from prefix
      param_type <- ""
      if (grepl("^bs_", p)) {
        param_type <- "Boundary (a)"
        p <- gsub("^bs_", "", p)
      } else if (grepl("^bias_", p)) {
        param_type <- "Bias (z)"
        p <- gsub("^bias_", "", p)
      } else if (grepl("^ndt_", p)) {
        param_type <- "Non-decision time (t_0)"
        p <- gsub("^ndt_", "", p)
      } else if (grepl("^b_", p)) {
        param_type <- "Drift (v)"
        p <- gsub("^b_", "", p)
      } else {
        # Try to infer from content
        if (grepl("bs|boundary", orig, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
          param_type <- "Boundary (a)"
        } else if (grepl("ndt|non.decision", orig, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
          param_type <- "Non-decision time (t_0)"
        } else if (grepl("bias", orig, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
          param_type <- "Bias (z)"
        } else {
          param_type <- "Drift (v)"  # Default
        }
      }
      
      # Handle Intercept
      if (p == "Intercept" || orig == "Intercept") {
        result[i] <- paste0(param_type, ": Intercept")
        next
      }
      
      # Handle task-specific parameters that are already formatted (e.g., "Drift (v): ADT")
      # These come from the updated extraction script that computes task-specific intercepts
      if (grepl(": (ADT|VDT)$", orig, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
        result[i] <- orig  # Pass through already-formatted task-specific parameters
        next
      }
      
      # Step 1: Check if this is an interaction (has colon between different factors in raw R format)
      # Interactions have colons between factor patterns like difficulty_level:task or effort_condition:task
      is_raw_interaction <- grepl("_level:", p) || grepl("_condition:", p) || 
                           (grepl("difficulty_level", p) && grepl(":task", p)) ||
                           (grepl("effort_condition", p) && grepl(":task", p)) ||
                           (grepl("difficulty_level", p) && grepl(":effort_condition", p))
      
      if (is_raw_interaction) {
        # Handle interactions: split by colon between factors, clean each part, join with ×
        # Pattern: difficulty_levelHard:taskVDT -> split -> clean -> "Difficulty: Hard × Task: VDT"
        if (grepl(":", p) && !grepl(" × ", p)) {
          # Split by colon (assuming only one colon between factors for interactions)
          parts <- strsplit(p, ":")[[1]]
          # Clean each part
          cleaned_parts <- character(length(parts))
          for (j in seq_along(parts)) {
            part <- parts[j]
            # Clean difficulty
            part <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy", "Difficulty: Easy", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            part <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard", "Difficulty: Hard", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            part <- gsub("difficulty_levelStandard", "Difficulty: Standard", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            # Clean task
            part <- gsub("^taskVDT$", "Task: VDT", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            part <- gsub("^taskADT$", "Task: ADT", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            # Clean effort
            part <- gsub("^effort_conditionLow_Force_5pct$", "Effort: Low", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            part <- gsub("^effort_conditionLow_MVC$", "Effort: Low", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            part <- gsub("^effort_conditionLow$", "Effort: Low", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            part <- gsub("^effort_conditionHigh_Force_40pct$", "Effort: High", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            part <- gsub("^effort_conditionHigh_MVC$", "Effort: High", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            part <- gsub("^effort_conditionHigh$", "Effort: High", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            cleaned_parts[j] <- part
          }
          # Join with ×
          p <- paste(cleaned_parts, collapse = " × ")
        }
      } else {
        # Step 2: Main effects - clean normally (preserve colons)
      # Clean difficulty levels (flexible matching)
      p <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy", "Difficulty: Easy", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      p <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard", "Difficulty: Hard", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      p <- gsub("difficulty_levelStandard", "Difficulty: Standard", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      
      # Clean task
      p <- gsub("taskVDT", "Task: VDT", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      p <- gsub("taskADT", "Task: ADT", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      
      # Clean effort conditions (handle all variations - order matters!)
      p <- gsub("effort_conditionLow_Force_5pct", "Effort: Low", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      p <- gsub("effort_conditionLow_MVC", "Effort: Low", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      p <- gsub("effort_conditionLow", "Effort: Low", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      p <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh_Force_40pct", "Effort: High", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      p <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh_MVC", "Effort: High", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      p <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh", "Effort: High", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      }
      
      # Add parameter type prefix if we have meaningful content
      if (p != orig && param_type != "") {
        # Check if param already starts with a parameter type (avoid duplication)
        if (!grepl("^(Drift|Boundary|Non-decision|Bias)", p)) {
          result[i] <- paste0(param_type, ": ", p)
        } else {
          result[i] <- p
        }
      } else {
        result[i] <- p
      }
    }
    
    return(result)
  }
  
  sens_subchance <- sensitivity_summary %>%
    filter(sensitivity == "exclude_subchance") %>%
    mutate(
      model_clean = clean_model_name(model),
      parameter_clean = clean_ddm_parameter(parameter),
      across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 3))
    ) %>%
    select(model_clean, parameter_clean, baseline_estimate, sensitivity_estimate, delta, 
           delta_ci_lower, delta_ci_upper, ci_overlap, delta_contains_zero) %>%
    rename(model = model_clean, parameter = parameter_clean) %>%
    arrange(model, parameter)
  
  if (nrow(sens_subchance) > 0) {
    sens_subchance %>%
      gt() %>%
      cols_label(
        model = "Model",
        parameter = "Parameter",
        baseline_estimate = "Baseline",
        sensitivity_estimate = "Excluded",
        delta = "Δ",
        delta_ci_lower = "Δ CI Lower",
        delta_ci_upper = "Δ CI Upper",
        ci_overlap = "CI Overlap",
        delta_contains_zero = "Δ Contains 0"
      ) %>%
      tab_footnote(
        footnote = "Baseline: N=67 (includes sub-chance). Excluded: N=55 (excludes sub-chance). Δ = Excluded - Baseline. If Δ CI contains 0 and CIs overlap, parameter is robust.",
        locations = cells_column_labels(columns = delta_contains_zero)
      ) %>%
      tab_source_note(
        source_note = paste0("Data: output/checks/sensitivity_summary.csv. ",
          if (file.exists(file.path(proj_root, "output/checks/sensitivity_summary.csv")))
            paste0("Last modified ", format(file.info(file.path(proj_root, "output/checks/sensitivity_summary.csv"))$mtime, "%Y-%m-%d"), ". ")
          else "",
          "Refresh: Rscript scripts/checks/sensitivity.R")
      ) %>%
      opt_table_font(size = "small") %>%
      tab_options(
        table.width = pct(90),
        table.font.size = px(9),
        column_labels.font.size = px(10),
        column_labels.padding = px(8),
        data_row.padding = px(6),
        table_body.hlines.width = px(0.5),
        table_body.vlines.width = px(0.5),
        table.border.top.width = px(1.5),
        table.border.bottom.width = px(1.5)
      ) %>%
      tab_style(
        style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
        locations = cells_column_labels()
      )
  } else {
    tibble(Note = "No sensitivity data available.") %>%
      knitr::kable(format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"), booktabs = TRUE) %>%
      kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position", full_width = FALSE)
  }
} else {
  tibble(Note = "Sensitivity summary data not loaded.") %>%
    knitr::kable(format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"), booktabs = TRUE) %>%
    kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position", full_width = FALSE)
}
```

```{=latex}
\end{landscape}
```

**Results**: Most key parameters showed robust estimates when excluding sub-chance participants. For Model3_Difficulty and Model4_Additive, the drift intercept and boundary separation showed delta CIs that included zero, indicating no meaningful change. The Easy difficulty effect was also robust. The Hard difficulty effect showed a small shift ($\Delta \approx -0.10$, delta CI did not include zero), but this represents a small change in magnitude (approximately 6.5% of the baseline estimate) and does not alter the substantive conclusion that Hard trials show negative drift relative to Standard. 

**Conclusion**: Sensitivity analyses confirmed that inclusion of these participants did not alter the pattern of main effects. The inclusion of sub-chance participants did not meaningfully alter main effects or substantive conclusions, supporting our decision to retain all 67 participants to maximize sample size and leverage hierarchical modeling's ability to stabilize estimates through shrinkage.

### A4.2 RT Cutoff Thresholds {.unnumbered}

We tested sensitivity to the minimum cue-locked RT cutoff (0.15 s, 0.20 s, 0.25 s) to ensure conclusions do not depend on the specific threshold choice. @tbl-sensitivity-thresholds summarizes trial retention and model fit (LOOIC) across thresholds. Parameter estimates were robust across all three cutoffs, with 95% credible interval overlap for all key contrasts (detailed parameter tables in subsequent figures). Raw LOOIC values differ across thresholds (different trial counts: 17,981 at 0.15 s vs 17,720 at 0.25 s) and are not directly comparable; we evaluate sensitivity by parameter stability across cutoffs rather than by LOOIC selection. Parameter estimates for key contrasts remained stable across all three cutoffs (95% CrI overlap), confirming that substantive conclusions are robust to threshold choice. We adopted 0.20 s as the primary cutoff, balancing exclusion of implausibly fast guesses with trial retention.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-app-sensitivity-full
#| tbl-cap: "Full sensitivity analysis results across RT cutoffs (0.15, 0.20, 0.25 s)."
#| tbl-pos: "htbp"

# Print full tbl_sens table
if (!is.null(tbl_sens) && nrow(tbl_sens) > 0) {
  tbl_sens %>%
    arrange(threshold) %>%
    mutate(
      across(where(is.numeric) & !matches("threshold"), ~round(.x, 3))
    ) %>%
    knitr::kable(format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"), 
                 booktabs = TRUE, 
                 linesep = "") %>%
    kableExtra::kable_styling(
      latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position", "scale_down"),
      bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"),
      full_width = FALSE
    )
} else {
  invisible(NULL)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-app-sensitivity-looic

  # Add looic_se if missing
  if (!"looic_se" %in% names(tbl_sens)) {
    tbl_sens <- tbl_sens %>% mutate(looic_se = NA_real_)
  }
  ggplot(tbl_sens, aes(x = threshold, y = looic)) +
    geom_point(size = 1.8) +
    {if (!all(is.na(tbl_sens$looic_se))) geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = looic - looic_se, ymax = looic + looic_se), width = 0.01)} +
    geom_line(alpha = 0.5) +

      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
} else {
```

### A4.3 Task Modality Effects: Sensitivity Analysis {.unnumbered}

The primary model (Table 8) excluded Task (ADT vs. VDT) as a predictor for drift rate ($v$) and boundary separation ($a$) to reduce model complexity. Peer reviewers noted that auditory and visual processing speeds differ psychophysically, and pooling these modalities may mask Task main effects or Effort × Task interactions. To address this, we fit a **task-sensitivity model** with:

- Drift rate ($v$): `~ difficulty + effort * task` (with interaction)
- Boundary separation ($a$): `~ difficulty + effort + task` (main effects only)
- All other parameters unchanged from the primary model

#### Drift Rate by Task {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: fig-suppl-drift-by-task
#| fig-cap: "**Supplementary Figure 1.** Drift rate ($v$) by difficulty and effort, separately for ADT and VDT. Points show posterior medians with 95% credible intervals. The difficulty gradient (Standard $<$ Hard $<$ Easy) is consistent across tasks. High effort reduces drift rate in both modalities (no significant Effort $\\times$ Task interaction), confirming that cognitive-motor interference generalizes across sensory domains. *Note: Drift rates ($v$) were estimated using Response Coding. Positive values indicate evidence accumulation toward the 'Different' boundary; negative values indicate accumulation toward the 'Same' boundary.*"
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-pos: "htbp"
#| out-width: "75%"

drift_plot_data_suppl <- pred_params %>%
  filter(model == PRIMARY_MODEL, rt_type == PRIMARY_RT, threshold == PRIMARY_THR) %>%
  mutate(
    difficulty = factor(difficulty, levels = c("Standard", "Easy", "Hard")),
    effort = factor(effort, levels = c("Low", "High")),
    task = factor(task, levels = c("ADT", "VDT"))
  )
if ("drift_estimate" %in% names(drift_plot_data_suppl)) {
  drift_plot_data_suppl <- drift_plot_data_suppl %>%
    mutate(drift_val = drift_estimate, drift_lower = if ("drift_low" %in% names(.)) drift_low else drift_q2.5, drift_upper = if ("drift_high" %in% names(.)) drift_high else drift_q97.5)
} else {
  drift_plot_data_suppl <- drift_plot_data_suppl %>%
    mutate(drift_val = drift_median, drift_lower = drift_q2.5, drift_upper = drift_q97.5)
}

p_drift_cond <- ggplot(drift_plot_data_suppl, aes(x = difficulty, y = drift_val, color = effort, group = effort)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = drift_lower, ymax = drift_upper), position = position_dodge(width = 0.3), size = 0.6) +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(width = 0.3), alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ task, labeller = labeller(task = c("ADT" = "ADT", "VDT" = "VDT"))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Low" = "#5DADE2", "High" = "#A23B72"), name = "Effort") +
  labs(x = "Difficulty", y = "Drift Rate (v)", title = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom", strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", color = NA)) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE)

print(p_drift_cond)
```

#### Boundary Separation by Task {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: fig-suppl-boundary-by-task
#| fig-cap: "**Supplementary Figure 2.** Boundary separation ($a$) by difficulty and effort, separately for ADT and VDT. Points show posterior medians with 95% credible intervals. Difficulty strongly modulates caution (Easy $<$ Standard $<$ Hard) in both tasks, but effort has minimal effect on boundary separation, indicating that older adults do not adjust response caution under physical effort."
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-pos: "htbp"
#| out-width: "75%"

boundary_plot_data_suppl <- pred_params %>%
  filter(model == PRIMARY_MODEL, rt_type == PRIMARY_RT, threshold == PRIMARY_THR) %>%
  mutate(
    difficulty = factor(difficulty, levels = c("Standard", "Easy", "Hard")),
    effort = factor(effort, levels = c("Low", "High")),
    task = factor(task, levels = c("ADT", "VDT"))
  )
if ("bs_estimate" %in% names(boundary_plot_data_suppl)) {
  boundary_plot_data_suppl <- boundary_plot_data_suppl %>%
    mutate(bs_val = bs_estimate, bs_lower = if ("bs_low" %in% names(.)) bs_low else a_q2.5, bs_upper = if ("bs_high" %in% names(.)) bs_high else a_q97.5)
} else if ("a_estimate" %in% names(boundary_plot_data_suppl)) {
  boundary_plot_data_suppl <- boundary_plot_data_suppl %>%
    mutate(bs_val = a_estimate, bs_lower = if ("a_low" %in% names(.)) a_low else a_q2.5, bs_upper = if ("a_high" %in% names(.)) a_high else a_q97.5)
} else {
  boundary_plot_data_suppl <- boundary_plot_data_suppl %>%
    mutate(bs_val = a_median, bs_lower = a_q2.5, bs_upper = a_q97.5)
}

p_boundary_cond <- ggplot(boundary_plot_data_suppl, aes(x = difficulty, y = bs_val, color = effort, group = effort)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = bs_lower, ymax = bs_upper), position = position_dodge(width = 0.3), size = 0.6) +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(width = 0.3), alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ task, labeller = labeller(task = c("ADT" = "ADT", "VDT" = "VDT"))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Low" = "#5DADE2", "High" = "#A23B72"), name = "Effort") +
  labs(x = "Difficulty", y = "Boundary Separation (a)", title = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom", strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", color = NA)) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE)

print(p_boundary_cond)
```

#### Task-Sensitivity Model Comparison {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-task-sensitivity
#| tbl-cap: "Comparison of Effort Effects: Primary vs. Task-Sensitivity Model"
#| tbl-pos: "htbp"
task_sens_path <- file.path(proj_root, params$run_dir, "tables", "task_sensitivity_comparison.csv")
if (file.exists(task_sens_path)) {
  task_sens_comp <- read_csv(task_sens_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  task_sens_comp %>%
    mutate(
      `95% CrI` = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", CI_lower, CI_upper),
      Estimate = sprintf("%.3f", Estimate)
    ) %>%
    select(Parameter, Estimate, `95% CrI`) %>%
    knitr::kable(booktabs = TRUE) %>%
    kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position") %>%
    kableExtra::add_footnote(
      "Note. Primary model excludes Task from drift; Task-Sens model includes Task main effect and Effort×Task interaction.",
      notation = "none"
    )
} else {
  cat("Task-sensitivity comparison table not yet available. Run the full DDM refit pipeline to generate it.")
}
```

The task-sensitivity model confirmed that the Effort → Drift effect was robust to inclusion of Task modality as a predictor ($\delta \approx -0.085$, 95% CrI $[-0.133, -0.038]$; same direction and credibility as the primary model). A credible Task main effect was observed ($\delta \approx 0.071$, 95% CrI $[0.020, 0.120]$), indicating that auditory and visual tasks differed modestly in absolute drift rates. However, the Effort $\times$ Task interaction was negligible ($\delta \approx 0.029$, 95% CrI $[-0.029, 0.088]$), confirming that cognitive-motor interference under High effort manifested similarly across sensory modalities. These results support the primary model's decision to pool ADT and VDT for main analyses, and validate the generalizability of the core drift rate finding across stimulus modalities.

```{r pdf-sanity-check}
#| include: false
#| eval: false
# Post-render PDF sanity check: verify no unresolved crossrefs remain
# To enable: change eval to true (or run manually after rendering)
# Requires: pdftotext (part of poppler-utils package)
# 
# This check prevents accidentally distributing PDFs with broken crossrefs.
# If any unresolved refs are found, the build will fail with a clear error message.

pdf_file <- "chap3_ddm_results.pdf"

if (file.exists(pdf_file)) {
  # Extract text from PDF
  pdf_text <- system2("pdftotext", args = c(pdf_file, "-"), stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE)
  
  # Check for unresolved crossrefs
  unresolved_patterns <- c(
    "Table \\?\\?",
    "Figure \\?\\?",
    "\\?@fig-",
    "\\?@tbl-",
    "\\?@sec-"
  )
  
  matches <- character(0)
  for (pattern in unresolved_patterns) {
    pattern_matches <- grep(pattern, pdf_text, value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)
    if (length(pattern_matches) > 0) {
      matches <- c(matches, pattern_matches)
    }
  }
  
  if (length(matches) > 0) {
    cat("ERROR: Unresolved crossrefs found in PDF:\n\n")
    for (match in unique(matches)) {
      cat("  ", match, "\n")
    }
    cat("\nFix the broken references above before distributing the PDF.\n")
    stop("Unresolved crossrefs remain in PDF. Build failed.", call. = FALSE)
  } else {
    cat("✓ PDF sanity check PASSED: No unresolved crossrefs found.\n")
  }
} else {
  warning("PDF file not found: ", pdf_file, ". Run this check after rendering.")
}
```


## A5. Pupil-DDM Fixed Effects (Link Scale) {#app-pupil-fixef .unnumbered}

Full parameter tables for the pupil-linked DDM confirm that global TEPR effects on drift rate and starting-point bias were near zero (posterior means near zero, 95% CrIs including zero; @tbl-pupil-key-effects). Model comparison via LOO-CV did not favor pooled pupil-augmented models over the behavioral baseline (Section 3.6); Pareto-$k$ diagnostics (max $k$ = 0.91) indicate PSIS-LOO estimates may be unreliable, so conclusions rest on posterior coefficient distributions. The primary inferential figure is @fig-pupil-drift-difficulty-interaction, which shows difficulty-conditional posterior slopes of `pupil_scaled` on drift rate from the `pupil_scaled * difficulty` interaction model. Complete coefficient tables are available in the online supplement at [https://github.com/mohdasti/modeling-pupil-DDM](https://github.com/mohdasti/modeling-pupil-DDM).

\newpage


## A6. Detailed DDM Model Specification {#sec-appendix-a6 .unnumbered}

This appendix provides the full mathematical specification of the hierarchical Wiener DDM, including link functions, prior distributions, and computational details omitted from the main Methods for brevity.

### A6.1 Link Functions and Parameter Constraints {.unnumbered}

**Link functions**: To ensure parameter constraints, we apply link functions [@ratcliff2002estimating; @burkner2017brms]. The model was implemented using the `brms` package with `family = wiener(link_bs="log", link_ndt="log", link_bias="logit")`: drift rate $v = \beta_v$ (identity link); boundary separation $a = \exp(\beta_{\text{bs}})$ (log link, ensures $a > 0$); non-decision time $t_0 = \exp(\beta_{\text{ndt}})$ (log link, ensures $t_0 > 0$); starting-point bias $z = \text{logit}^{-1}(\beta_{\text{bias}}) = \frac{\exp(\beta_{\text{bias}})}{1 + \exp(\beta_{\text{bias}})}$ (logit link, ensures $z \in [0,1]$).

### A6.2 Hierarchical Model Structure {.unnumbered}

For subject \(i\) and trial \(j\), the latent parameters follow:

**Hierarchical structure**: For subject $i$ and trial $j$, the model parameters are specified as [@burkner2017brms; @ratcliff2008diffusion]:

$$v_{ij} = \beta_{v,0} + \sum_k \beta_{v,k} X_{k,ij} + u_{v,i}$$ {#eq-drift-hierarchical}

$$a_{ij} = \exp\left(\beta_{\text{bs},0} + \sum_k \beta_{\text{bs},k} X_{k,ij} + u_{\text{bs},i}\right)$$ {#eq-boundary-hierarchical}

$$t_{0,ij} = \exp\left(\beta_{\text{ndt},0} + \sum_k \beta_{\text{ndt},k} X_{k,ij}\right)$$ {#eq-ndt-hierarchical}

$$z_{ij} = \text{logit}^{-1}\left(\beta_{\text{bias},0} + \sum_k \beta_{\text{bias},k} X_{k,ij} + u_{\text{bias},i}\right)$$ {#eq-bias-hierarchical}

where $\beta_{0}$ are population-level intercepts, $\beta_k$ are population-level coefficients for predictors $X_k$ (e.g., task, effort condition, difficulty level), and $u_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2_u)$ are subject-level random effects. Note that $t_0$ is modeled without subject-level random effects to maintain model stability in the response-signal design.

**Likelihood**: The likelihood for a single trial with RT $t$ and decision $d \in \{\text{"same"}, \text{"different"}\}$ follows the Wiener first-passage time distribution [@feller1968introduction]:

$$p(t, d | v, a, t_0, z) = \text{Wiener}(t - t_0 | v, a, z)$$ {#eq-likelihood}

where the Wiener distribution gives the probability density of the first-passage time to boundary $d$ given drift $v$, boundary separation $a$, and starting point $z \cdot a$.

The `brms` model formula for the Standard-only calibration model is specified as:

Parameter-specific formulas were: drift (v): `rt | dec(dec_upper) ~ 1 + (1|subject_id)` with relaxed prior N(0, 2) to allow potential negative drift; boundary (bs): `bs ~ 1 + (1|subject_id)`; non-decision time (ndt): `ndt ~ 1` (intercept-only); bias (z): `bias ~ task + effort_condition + (1|subject_id)`. These formulas comprise one model fitted simultaneously using `brms`'s `bf()` function.

The causal assumptions and hierarchical generative structure for the primary DDM are illustrated in the following figure:

To clarify the assumptions behind our RT definition, gating delay, and exclusion rules, we summarize the causal structure of the response-signal design and the hierarchical DDM in @fig-ddm-dag-plate. Panel A depicts a conceptual causal diagram in which Age and experimentally manipulated task factors (difficulty, modality, effort) influence latent DDM parameters, the wait constraint changes how latent decision completion maps onto observed RT, and RT-based exclusion is represented as conditioning on a selection node $S$. Panel B shows the corresponding generative structure of the hierarchical Wiener DDM, with subject-level parameters $v_i$, $a_i$, $T_{er,i}$ and trial-level predictors $X_{it}$ (difficulty, modality, effort) that generate choices and RTs. This figure separates our substantive causal assumptions from the statistical model used for estimation and highlights why RT cutoffs are treated as a potential source of selection bias in subsequent analyses.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ddm-dag-plate
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Causal assumptions and generative structure for the hierarchical DDM. Panel A shows a conceptual causal DAG in which Age and experimentally manipulated task factors (difficulty, modality, effort) influence latent DDM parameters under a gated-response design; the wait constraint alters the mapping from decision completion to observed RT, and trial selection S represents RT-based exclusions. Panel B shows the corresponding hierarchical generative structure: subject-level parameters $v_i$, $a_i$, $T_{er,i}$ are depicted as influenced by a generic subject-level covariate (e.g., Age_i), while in the present chapter age is not explicitly modeled because all participants are older adults; trial-level predictors $X_{it}$ (difficulty, modality, effort) modulate drift, and choices and RTs are generated from these parameters."
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-pos: "htbp"
#| out-width: "75%"
include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig-ddm-dag-plate-2.png"))
```


The complete `brms` formula syntax for the standard-only calibration model is:

```r
bf(rt | dec(dec_upper) ~ 1 + (1 | subject_id),
   bs ~ task + effort_condition + (1 | subject_id),
   ndt ~ 1,
   bias ~ task + effort_condition + (1 | subject_id),
   family = wiener(link_bs = "log",
                   link_ndt = "log",
                   link_bias = "logit"))
```

The complete `brms` formula syntax for the primary additive model is:

```r
bf(rt | dec(dec_upper) ~ difficulty_level + effort_condition +
                          (1 | subject_id),
   bs ~ difficulty_level + effort_condition + (1 | subject_id),
   ndt ~ 1,
   bias ~ task + effort_condition + (1 | subject_id),
   family = wiener(link_bs = "log",
                   link_ndt = "log",
                   link_bias = "logit"))
```

where `dec(dec_upper)` encodes the response boundary (1 = *different*, 0 = *same*), `bs` is the log-link parameter for boundary separation $a$, `ndt` is the log-link parameter for non-decision time $t_0$, and `bias` is the logit-link parameter for starting-point $z$.

### A6.3 Prior Specification {.unnumbered}

All priors were weakly informative and specified on the link scale. The table below summarizes the complete prior distribution for each parameter class.

**Priors.** All priors were weakly informative and specified on the link scale. For intercepts, drift rate ($v$) used Normal(0, 1); boundary separation ($a$) used Normal(log(1.3), 0.25), corresponding to $a \approx 1.3$ on the natural scale; non-decision time ($t_0$) used Normal(log(0.35), 0.15), corresponding to $t_0 \approx 0.35$ s on the natural scale (probe-onset-locked timing; the cue-locked variant used Normal(log(0.10), 0.15)); and starting-point bias ($z$) used Normal(0, 0.5), corresponding to $z \approx 0.5$ (no bias) on the probability scale. For slope parameters, drift rate slopes used Normal(0, 0.6–0.7), boundary separation slopes used Normal(0, 0.25–0.30), and bias slopes used Normal(0, 0.35). Random effects were assigned Student-t(3, 0, 0.30) priors for standard deviations and LKJ(2) priors for correlations. Prior versus posterior distributions for $t_0$ are shown in Supplementary @fig-ndt-prior-posterior, confirming adequate identifiability for the group-level intercept despite the response-signal design.

### A6.4 Computational Details {.unnumbered}

**Computational implementation.** All analyses were performed in R [@R] using `brms` [@burkner2017brms; @burkner2018brms] with CmdStan [@cmdstan2024] via `cmdstanr` [@cmdstanr]. Model fitting was conducted on a cloud compute instance (Google Cloud Platform) to accommodate the computational demands of hierarchical Wiener models. Model comparison used leave-one-out cross-validation via `loo` [@vehtari2017loo]. Data processing used the tidyverse suite [@dplyr; @tidyr; @readr; @wickham2016ggplot2], tables were generated with `gt` [@gt], and posterior analysis used `posterior` [@burkner2022posterior]. The manuscript was rendered using Quarto [@quarto].

**MCMC sampling.** Models were estimated using the No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS) [@hoffman2014nuts] with 8 parallel chains, each run for 2,000 iterations (1,000 warmup, 1,000 sampling). Within-chain parallelism was enabled (4 threads per chain) to accelerate sampling on a multi-core compute instance. Sampling controls were set to adapt_delta = 0.95 and max_treedepth = 12 to balance convergence and efficiency. Convergence was assessed using $\hat{R}$ $\leq$ 1.01 [@gelman1992inference; @vehtari2021rank] and minimum bulk effective sample size (ESS) $\geq$ 400. Trace plots were visually inspected for all parameters, and divergent transitions were monitored. Pre-specified convergence criteria required maximum $\hat{R}$ $\leq$ 1.01, minimum bulk and tail ESS $\geq$ 400, and zero divergent transitions. All reported models satisfied these criteria (maximum $\hat{R} < 1.01$, minimum ESS $> 1200$, zero divergences).

**Model comparison.** We compared a small set of pre-specified behavioral DDM variants differing in (i) parameterization of experimental effects (baseline vs. additive) and (ii) RT timing convention (cue-locked vs. probe-onset-locked). Models were compared using Pareto-smoothed importance sampling leave-one-out cross-validation (PSIS-LOO) via the loo package [@vehtari2017loo]. We report expected log predictive density (ELPD) and its standard error, with model differences assessed using `loo_compare()`, which computes the standard error of the ELPD difference accounting for correlations between models fitted to the same data [@vehtari2017loo]. Differences in ELPD exceeding 4 are considered meaningful (approximately equivalent to Δ LOOIC > 8). Pareto-k diagnostics were inspected to assess reliability of PSIS-LOO approximations. The LOO comparison table is presented in Results (@tbl-loo-comparison), with the full comparison plot in Appendix~A1 (@fig-loo-comparison).

**PSIS diagnostics.** We assessed the reliability of LOO estimates using Pareto-k diagnostics. Following Vehtari et al. [-@vehtari2017loo], we flagged observations with $k > 0.7$ as potentially problematic for PSIS approximation. When aggregate Pareto-$k_{\max}$ exceeded 0.7, we report model comparisons with appropriate caution and prioritize parameter-level inference over model selection.

**Posterior predictive checks.** Model fit was evaluated using posterior predictive checks (PPC), including subject-level and unconditional comparisons between observed and predicted data. PPC diagnostics included quantile-probability (QP) plots, Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) statistics, and residual heatmaps. Pre-declared PPC thresholds were: subject-wise mid-body QP RMSE $\leq$ 0.09 s, |Δ accuracy| $\leq$ 0.05, KS statistic $\leq$ 0.15, and $\leq$ 15% of cells flagged. We distinguish between **convergence diagnostics** ($\hat{R}$, ESS, divergences), which must be strictly satisfied for valid inference, and **posterior predictive fit quality**, which indicates where the model systematically deviates from data. PPC deviations in regions with sparse data (fast/slow tails) do not invalidate parameter estimates if key contrasts are robust to these deviations. We report both strict threshold-based PPC metrics (Appendix~A3, @tbl-convergence-ppc-gate-appendix) and visual diagnostics (QP plots, RT overlays; Appendix~A3.2, @fig-ch3app-ppc-rt-overlay) to provide a complete assessment.


## A7. Manipulation Checks: Behavioral Validation {#sec-appendix-a7 .unnumbered}

To confirm that the difficulty and effort manipulations produced the expected behavioral effects prior to and independent of DDM estimation, we conducted mixed-effects analyses on accuracy and RT. These analyses are reported here as pre-modeling validation; primary DDM results do not depend on them.

### A7.1 Statistical Models {.unnumbered}

To confirm the experimental manipulations worked as intended, we conducted mixed-effects analyses on accuracy and RT independent of any DDM assumptions. These analyses serve to validate that the experimental design successfully manipulated difficulty and effort conditions before proceeding to DDM parameter estimation.

**Accuracy analysis.** Accuracy was modeled using mixed-effects logistic regression (generalized linear mixed model, GLMM) with fixed effects for difficulty, effort, and task (including interactions as needed), and random intercepts for subject. Analyses were restricted to Easy and Hard trials only (excluding Standard trials), as the difficulty manipulation is only meaningful within "different" trials where stimulus offsets vary.

**Reaction time analysis.** Reaction time was modeled using mixed-effects linear regression on cue-locked RT (median RT per subject-condition), with the same fixed and random effects structure as the accuracy model. Standard trials were excluded to focus on trials where difficulty manipulation is meaningful.

Full results are reported in Sections A7.2 and A7.3 below.

```{r mc-sample-size}
#| echo: false
#| include: false
# Compute manipulation checks sample size for inline use
n_trials_mc <- 13771L
if (!is.null(behavioral_data)) {
  diff_col <- intersect(c("difficulty_level", "difficulty"), names(behavioral_data))[1]
  if (!is.null(diff_col)) {
    mc_data_count <- behavioral_data %>%
      filter(tolower(as.character(!!sym(diff_col))) %in% c("easy", "hard"))
    n_trials_mc <- nrow(mc_data_count)
  }
}
```

### A7.2 Accuracy and RT Results {.unnumbered}

We confirmed that the difficulty and effort manipulations affected performance as intended using mixed-effects models independent of DDM assumptions, restricted to Easy and Hard trials (N = `r format(n_trials_mc, big.mark = ",")`).

```{r}
#| include: false
# Compute accuracy means for narrative (same data as Figure 7 and GLMM)
acc_means_for_narrative <- NULL
acc_hard_min <- 26.4
acc_hard_mean <- 30.5
acc_easy_mean <- 85.2
acc_high_mean <- 56.8
acc_low_mean <- 58.5
if (!is.null(behavioral_data)) {
  acc_col <- intersect(c("correct", "iscorr", "accuracy"), names(behavioral_data))[1]
  diff_col <- intersect(c("difficulty_level", "difficulty"), names(behavioral_data))[1]
  effort_col <- intersect(c("effort_condition", "effort"), names(behavioral_data))[1]
  task_col <- intersect(c("task", "Task"), names(behavioral_data))[1]
  if (!is.null(acc_col) && !is.null(diff_col)) {
    mc_data <- behavioral_data %>%
      filter(tolower(as.character(!!sym(diff_col))) %in% c("easy", "hard"))
    if (nrow(mc_data) > 0) {
      acc_means_for_narrative <- mc_data %>%
        mutate(diff = ifelse(tolower(as.character(!!sym(diff_col))) == "easy", "Easy", "Hard")) %>%
        group_by(diff) %>%
        summarise(mean_acc = mean(!!sym(acc_col), na.rm = TRUE) * 100, .groups = "drop")
      acc_hard_mean <- round(acc_means_for_narrative %>% filter(diff == "Hard") %>% pull(mean_acc), 1)
      acc_easy_mean <- round(acc_means_for_narrative %>% filter(diff == "Easy") %>% pull(mean_acc), 1)
      if (!is.null(effort_col) && effort_col %in% names(mc_data)) {
        effort_means <- mc_data %>%
          mutate(effort = tolower(as.character(!!sym(effort_col)))) %>%
          mutate(effort = ifelse(grepl("high|40", effort), "High", "Low")) %>%
          group_by(effort) %>%
          summarise(mean_acc = mean(!!sym(acc_col), na.rm = TRUE) * 100, .groups = "drop")
        acc_high_mean <- round(effort_means %>% filter(effort == "High") %>% pull(mean_acc), 1)
        acc_low_mean <- round(effort_means %>% filter(effort == "Low") %>% pull(mean_acc), 1)
      }
      if (!is.null(effort_col) && effort_col %in% names(mc_data) && !is.null(task_col) && task_col %in% names(mc_data)) {
        hard_cells <- mc_data %>%
          filter(tolower(as.character(!!sym(diff_col))) == "hard") %>%
          group_by(!!sym(task_col), !!sym(effort_col)) %>%
          summarise(mean_acc = mean(!!sym(acc_col), na.rm = TRUE) * 100, .groups = "drop")
        acc_hard_min <- round(min(hard_cells$mean_acc, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Hard trials were significantly less accurate than Easy trials, $\beta = -2.97$, 95% CI [−3.07, −2.88], $p < .001$, with mean accuracies of `r acc_hard_mean`% (Hard) and `r acc_easy_mean`% (Easy) (@tbl-accuracy-glmm, @fig-accuracy-distribution). Accuracy was lowest in Hard+High effort cells (`r acc_hard_min`%), indicating that difficulty and effort effects combine additively. High-effort trials showed lower accuracy than Low-effort trials ($\beta = -0.16$, 95% CI [−0.24, −0.07], $p < .001$), with mean accuracy of `r acc_high_mean`% (High) versus `r acc_low_mean`% (Low).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-accuracy-glmm
#| tbl-cap: "Accuracy GLMM Results"
if (!is.null(acc_glmm)) {
  # Function to clean up term names for publication (vectorized)
  clean_term_name <- function(term) {
    term <- as.character(term)
    
    # Intercept
    term <- ifelse(term == "(Intercept)", "Intercept", term)
    
    # Step 1: Handle interactions FIRST (on raw R terms)
    # Difficulty × Task interactions
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy:taskVDT", "Difficulty: Easy × Task: VDT", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy:taskADT", "Difficulty: Easy × Task: ADT", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard:taskVDT", "Difficulty: Hard × Task: VDT", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard:taskADT", "Difficulty: Hard × Task: ADT", term)
    
    # Effort × Task interactions
    term <- gsub("effort_conditionLow_5_MVC:taskVDT", "Effort: Low (5% MVC) × Task: VDT", term)
    term <- gsub("effort_conditionLow_5_MVC:taskADT", "Effort: Low (5% MVC) × Task: ADT", term)
    term <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh_MVC:taskVDT", "Effort: High (40% MVC) × Task: VDT", term)
    term <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh_MVC:taskADT", "Effort: High (40% MVC) × Task: ADT", term)
    term <- gsub("effort_conditionLow:taskVDT", "Effort: Low × Task: VDT", term)
    term <- gsub("effort_conditionLow:taskADT", "Effort: Low × Task: ADT", term)
    term <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh:taskVDT", "Effort: High × Task: VDT", term)
    term <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh:taskADT", "Effort: High × Task: ADT", term)
    
    # Difficulty × Effort interactions
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy:effort_conditionLow_5_MVC", "Difficulty: Easy × Effort: Low (5% MVC)", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy:effort_conditionHigh_MVC", "Difficulty: Easy × Effort: High (40% MVC)", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard:effort_conditionLow_5_MVC", "Difficulty: Hard × Effort: Low (5% MVC)", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard:effort_conditionHigh_MVC", "Difficulty: Hard × Effort: High (40% MVC)", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy:effort_conditionLow", "Difficulty: Easy × Effort: Low", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy:effort_conditionHigh", "Difficulty: Easy × Effort: High", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard:effort_conditionLow", "Difficulty: Hard × Effort: Low", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard:effort_conditionHigh", "Difficulty: Hard × Effort: High", term)
    
    # Step 2: Handle main effects (only for terms NOT already processed as interactions)
    # Check if term is NOT already an interaction (doesn't contain ×)
    main_effect_mask <- !grepl(" × ", term)
    
    # Main effects (preserve colons - these separate factor name from level)
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy", "Difficulty: Easy", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard", "Difficulty: Hard", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("effort_conditionLow_5_MVC", "Effort: Low", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh_MVC", "Effort: High", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("effort_conditionLow", "Effort: Low", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh", "Effort: High", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("taskVDT", "Task: VDT", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("taskADT", "Task: ADT", term[main_effect_mask])
    
    # Step 3: For any remaining raw R interactions (not caught above), convert colon to ×
    # Only if term still has raw R format colons (between factor names, not in cleaned format)
    raw_interaction_mask <- grepl("_condition|_level|task", term) & grepl(":", term) & !grepl(" × ", term)
    term[raw_interaction_mask] <- gsub(":", " × ", term[raw_interaction_mask])
    
    return(term)
  }
  
  acc_glmm %>%
    filter(effect == "fixed") %>%
    mutate(
      term_clean = clean_term_name(term),
      estimate_fmt = sprintf("%.2f", estimate),
      p_value_fmt = ifelse(p.value < .001, "<.001", sprintf("%.3f", p.value)),
      ci_fmt = sprintf("[%.2f, %.2f]", conf.low, conf.high)
    ) %>%
    select(term_clean, estimate_fmt, std.error, statistic, p_value_fmt, ci_fmt) %>%
    rename(term = term_clean) %>%
    gt() %>%
    cols_label(
      term = "Term",
      estimate_fmt = "Estimate",
      std.error = "SE",
      p_value_fmt = "p",
      ci_fmt = "95% CI"
    )
}
```

### A7.3 Reaction Time Results {.unnumbered}

```{r rt-medians-compute}
#| echo: false
#| include: false
# Compute median RTs for Hard and Easy for inline use
rt_hard_median <- 1.01
rt_easy_median <- 0.75
if (!is.null(behavioral_data)) {
  rt_col <- intersect(c("rt", "resp1RT", "RT"), names(behavioral_data))[1]
  diff_col <- intersect(c("difficulty_level", "difficulty"), names(behavioral_data))[1]
  if (!is.null(rt_col) && !is.null(diff_col)) {
    rt_by_diff <- behavioral_data %>%
      filter(!is.na(!!sym(rt_col)), !!sym(rt_col) > 0) %>%
      filter(tolower(as.character(!!sym(diff_col))) %in% c("easy", "hard")) %>%
      mutate(diff = ifelse(tolower(as.character(!!sym(diff_col))) == "easy", "Easy", "Hard")) %>%
      group_by(diff) %>%
      summarise(median_rt = median(!!sym(rt_col), na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
    if (nrow(rt_by_diff) > 0) {
      rt_hard_median <- round(rt_by_diff %>% filter(diff == "Hard") %>% pull(median_rt), 2)
      rt_easy_median <- round(rt_by_diff %>% filter(diff == "Easy") %>% pull(median_rt), 2)
    }
  }
}
```

Hard trials were slower than Easy trials, $\beta = 0.23 \,\text{s}$, 95% CI [0.20, 0.27], $p < .001$, with median RTs of `r rt_hard_median` s and `r rt_easy_median` s, respectively (@tbl-rt-lmm, @fig-rt-distribution). The effort manipulation did not reliably affect RT ($\beta = 0.02 \,\text{s}$, 95% CI [−0.02, 0.05]).

```{r}
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy:effort_conditionHigh_MVC", "Difficulty: Easy × Effort: High (40% MVC)", term)

    main_effect_mask <- !grepl(" × ", term)
    
    # Main effects (preserve colons - these separate factor name from level)
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy", "Difficulty: Easy", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard", "Difficulty: Hard", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("effort_conditionLow_5_MVC", "Effort: Low", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh_MVC", "Effort: High", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("effort_conditionLow", "Effort: Low", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh", "Effort: High", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("taskVDT", "Task: VDT", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("taskADT", "Task: ADT", term[main_effect_mask])

    raw_interaction_mask <- grepl("_condition|_level|task", term) & grepl(":", term) & !grepl(" × ", term)
    term[raw_interaction_mask] <- gsub(":", " × ", term[raw_interaction_mask])

  rt_lmm %>%
    filter(effect == "fixed") %>%
    mutate(

      estimate_fmt = sprintf("%.3f", estimate),

```

Difficulty reliably affected both accuracy ($\beta = -2.97$, 95% CI [−3.07, −2.88], $p < .001$) and RT ($\beta = 0.23$ s, 95% CI [0.20, 0.27], $p < .001$). Effort reduced accuracy ($\beta = -0.16$, 95% CI [−0.24, −0.07], $p < .001$) without reliably affecting RT ($\beta = 0.02$ s, 95% CI [−0.02, 0.05]). These patterns were consistent with successful experimental manipulation of perceptual difficulty and concurrent physical effort.

```{r overall-accuracy-compute}
#| echo: false
#| include: false
# Compute overall accuracy for inline use (Easy and Hard trials only, and all trials)
overall_acc_mean <- 63.5
overall_acc_sd <- 10.5
overall_acc_min <- 30.6
overall_acc_max <- 92.3
overall_acc_with_standard <- 70.1
if (!is.null(behavioral_data)) {
  acc_col <- intersect(c("correct", "iscorr", "accuracy"), names(behavioral_data))[1]
  diff_col <- intersect(c("difficulty_level", "difficulty"), names(behavioral_data))[1]
  subj_col <- intersect(c("subject_id", "sub"), names(behavioral_data))[1]
  if (!is.null(acc_col) && !is.null(diff_col) && !is.null(subj_col)) {
    # Easy and Hard only
    data_for_acc <- behavioral_data %>%
      filter(.data[[diff_col]] %in% c("Easy", "Hard"))
    overall_acc <- data_for_acc %>%
      group_by(!!sym(subj_col)) %>%
      summarise(accuracy = mean(!!sym(acc_col), na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
    if (nrow(overall_acc) > 0) {
      overall_acc_mean <- round(mean(overall_acc$accuracy, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1)
      overall_acc_sd <- round(sd(overall_acc$accuracy, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1)
      overall_acc_min <- round(min(overall_acc$accuracy, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1)
      overall_acc_max <- round(max(overall_acc$accuracy, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1)
    }
    # All trials (including Standard)
    overall_acc_all <- behavioral_data %>%
      group_by(!!sym(subj_col)) %>%
      summarise(accuracy = mean(!!sym(acc_col), na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
    if (nrow(overall_acc_all) > 0) {
      overall_acc_with_standard <- round(mean(overall_acc_all$accuracy, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1)
    }
  }
}
```

Across Easy and Hard trials, older adults showed moderate overall accuracy (*M* = `r overall_acc_mean`%, *SD* = `r overall_acc_sd`%; @tbl-overall-accuracy). When including Standard trials (which had near-perfect performance), overall accuracy was `r overall_acc_with_standard`%. Accuracy varied substantially across individuals (range = `r overall_acc_min`–`r overall_acc_max`%), consistent with the strong effects of difficulty and effort documented above.

```{r}
#| echo: false

# Compute accuracy by condition
if (!is.null(behavioral_data)) {
  # Standardize column names for accuracy
  if ("correct" %in% names(behavioral_data)) {
    acc_col <- "correct"
  } else if ("iscorr" %in% names(behavioral_data)) {
    acc_col <- "iscorr"
  } else if ("accuracy" %in% names(behavioral_data)) {
    acc_col <- "accuracy"
  } else {
    acc_col <- NULL
  }
  
  # Get task, difficulty, effort columns (already standardized above)
  if (!is.null(acc_col) && !is.null(task_col) && !is.null(diff_col) && !is.null(effort_col)) {
    # Get subject ID column
    subj_col <- if ("subject_id" %in% names(behavioral_data)) "subject_id" else if ("sub" %in% names(behavioral_data)) "sub" else NULL
    
    if (!is.null(subj_col)) {
      # Subject-level accuracy by condition
      acc_by_condition <- behavioral_data %>%
        group_by(!!sym(task_col), !!sym(diff_col), !!sym(effort_col), !!sym(subj_col)) %>%
        summarise(
          n_trials = n(),
          n_correct = sum(!!sym(acc_col), na.rm = TRUE),
          accuracy = mean(!!sym(acc_col), na.rm = TRUE),
          .groups = "drop"
        ) %>%
        group_by(!!sym(task_col), !!sym(diff_col), !!sym(effort_col)) %>%
        summarise(
          mean_acc = round(mean(accuracy, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1),
          sd_acc = round(sd(accuracy, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1),
          median_acc = round(median(accuracy, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1),
          min_acc = round(min(accuracy, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1),
          max_acc = round(max(accuracy, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1),
          n_subjects = n(),
          .groups = "drop"
        ) %>%
        # Clean up labels for display
        mutate(
          Task = case_when(
            !!sym(task_col) == "ADT" ~ "ADT",
            !!sym(task_col) == "VDT" ~ "VDT",
            TRUE ~ as.character(!!sym(task_col))
          ),
          Difficulty = case_when(
            !!sym(diff_col) == "Standard" ~ "Standard",
            !!sym(diff_col) == "Easy" ~ "Easy",
            !!sym(diff_col) == "Hard" ~ "Hard",
            TRUE ~ as.character(!!sym(diff_col))
          ),
          Effort = case_when(
            !!sym(effort_col) == "Low_5_MVC" ~ "Low (5% MVC)",
            !!sym(effort_col) == "High_40_MVC" ~ "High (40% MVC)",
            !!sym(effort_col) == "low" ~ "Low (5% MVC)",
            !!sym(effort_col) == "high" ~ "High (40% MVC)",
            TRUE ~ as.character(!!sym(effort_col))
          )
        )
    
    acc_table_data <- acc_by_condition %>%
      arrange(Task, Difficulty, Effort) %>%
      mutate(
        Task_Group = case_when(
          Task == "ADT" ~ "ADT (Auditory Detection Task)",
          Task == "VDT" ~ "VDT (Visual Detection Task)",
          TRUE ~ Task
        ),
        Difficulty = Difficulty,
        Effort = Effort,
        `Mean %` = mean_acc,
        `SD %` = sd_acc,
        `Median %` = median_acc,
        `Min %` = min_acc,
        `Max %` = max_acc,
        `N` = n_subjects
      ) %>%
      mutate(
        Task_Group = gsub("\u2013", "-", Task_Group),
        Difficulty = gsub("\u2013", "-", Difficulty),
        Effort = gsub("\u2013", "-", Effort)
      ) %>%
      select(Task_Group, Difficulty, Effort, `Mean %`, `SD %`, `Median %`, `Min %`, `Max %`, `N`)
    
    # Create gt table with row groups using groupname_col
    acc_table_data %>%
      gt(groupname_col = "Task_Group") %>%
      fmt_number(columns = where(is.numeric) & !matches("^N$"), decimals = 1) %>%
      fmt_number(columns = matches("^N$"), decimals = 0) %>%
      tab_style(
        style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
        locations = cells_column_labels()
      ) %>%
      tab_style(
        style = cell_text(weight = "bold", style = "italic"),
        locations = cells_row_groups()
      ) %>%
      tab_options(
        row_group.as_column = FALSE,
        row_group.padding = px(8)
      )
    } else {
      # Placeholder if subject column not found
      cat("**Accuracy Descriptives**:\n")
      cat("Subject ID column not found. Please ensure data contains: subject_id or sub\n")
    }
  } else {
    # Placeholder if columns not found
    cat("**Accuracy Descriptives**:\n")
    cat("Behavioral data columns not fully identified. Please ensure data contains: correct/iscorr/accuracy, task, difficulty_level, effort_condition, subject_id\n")
  }
} else {
  # Placeholder table with row grouping
  acc_placeholder <- expand_grid(
```

```{r}
  task_col <- intersect(c("task", "Task"), names(behavioral_data))[1]
  diff_col <- intersect(c("difficulty_level", "difficulty"), names(behavioral_data))[1]
  effort_col <- intersect(c("effort_condition", "effort"), names(behavioral_data))[1]
  subj_col <- intersect(c("subject_id", "sub"), names(behavioral_data))[1]
  
  if (!is.null(acc_col) && !is.null(task_col) && !is.null(diff_col) && !is.null(effort_col) && !is.null(subj_col)) {
    # Build data_long: subject-level mean accuracy by condition
    data_long <- behavioral_data %>%
      filter(!is.na(!!sym(acc_col))) %>%
      group_by(!!sym(subj_col), !!sym(task_col), !!sym(diff_col), !!sym(effort_col)) %>%
      summarise(mean_acc = mean(!!sym(acc_col), na.rm = TRUE) * 100, .groups = "drop") %>%
      transmute(
        subject_id = as.character(!!sym(subj_col)),
        task = case_when(
          !!sym(task_col) %in% c("ADT", "adt") ~ "ADT",
          !!sym(task_col) %in% c("VDT", "vdt") ~ "VDT",
          TRUE ~ as.character(!!sym(task_col))
        ),
        difficulty = case_when(
          !!sym(diff_col) %in% c("Standard", "standard") ~ "Standard",
          !!sym(diff_col) %in% c("Easy", "easy") ~ "Easy",
          !!sym(diff_col) %in% c("Hard", "hard") ~ "Hard",
          tolower(!!sym(diff_col)) == "easy" ~ "Easy",
          tolower(!!sym(diff_col)) == "hard" ~ "Hard",
          tolower(!!sym(diff_col)) == "standard" ~ "Standard",
          TRUE ~ as.character(!!sym(diff_col))
        ),
        effort = case_when(
          !!sym(effort_col) %in% c("Low_5_MVC", "low", "Low") ~ "Low",
          !!sym(effort_col) %in% c("High_40_MVC", "high", "High") ~ "High",
          TRUE ~ as.character(!!sym(effort_col))
        ),
        accuracy = mean_acc
      ) %>%
      mutate(
        task = factor(task, levels = c("ADT", "VDT")),
        difficulty = factor(difficulty, levels = c("Standard", "Easy", "Hard")),
        effort = factor(effort, levels = c("Low", "High"))
      )

    if (nrow(data_long) > 0) {
      # Cousineau-Morey within-subject SE: for each (task, difficulty), normalize by subject mean
      cm_se_by_cell <- data_long %>%
        group_by(task, difficulty, subject_id) %>%
        mutate(subj_mean = mean(accuracy, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
        ungroup() %>%
        group_by(task, difficulty) %>%
        mutate(grand_mean = mean(accuracy, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
        ungroup() %>%
        mutate(normalized = accuracy - subj_mean + grand_mean) %>%
        group_by(task, difficulty, effort) %>%
        summarise(
          mean_acc = mean(accuracy, na.rm = TRUE),
          n = n(),
          cm_se = sd(normalized, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n) * sqrt(2 / (2 - 1)),
          .groups = "drop"
        )
      # Diagnostic: compute cell means (as plotted) and marginal means (as in narrative)
      fig7_cell_means <- data_long %>%
        group_by(task, difficulty, effort) %>%
        summarise(mean_acc = mean(accuracy, na.rm = TRUE), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
      fig7_marginal_diff <- data_long %>%
        filter(difficulty %in% c("Hard", "Easy")) %>%
        group_by(difficulty) %>%
        summarise(marginal_mean = mean(accuracy, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
      effort_colors <- c("Low" = "#5DA5DA", "High" = "#B276B2")
      p1 <- ggplot(data_long, aes(x = effort, y = accuracy, group = subject_id)) +
        geom_line(alpha = 0.15, linewidth = 0.3, color = "gray40") +
        geom_point(aes(color = effort), alpha = 0.4, size = 0.9,
                  position = position_jitter(width = 0.05, seed = 42)) +
        stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun = mean, geom = "line",
                     linewidth = 0.8, color = "black") +
        stat_summary(aes(group = 1, fill = "Mean"), fun.data = function(x) ggplot2::mean_se(x, mult = 1.96),
                     geom = "ribbon", alpha = 0.2, color = NA) +
        geom_errorbar(data = cm_se_by_cell, aes(x = effort, y = mean_acc, ymin = mean_acc - 1.96 * cm_se, ymax = mean_acc + 1.96 * cm_se, group = effort),
                      inherit.aes = FALSE, width = 0.1, linewidth = 0.8, position = position_dodge(width = 0.2)) +
        geom_point(data = cm_se_by_cell, aes(x = effort, y = mean_acc, color = effort, group = effort),
                   inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 2, shape = 21, fill = "white", stroke = 1,
                   position = position_dodge(width = 0.2)) +
        facet_grid(task ~ difficulty,
                   labeller = labeller(
                     task = c(ADT = "Auditory", VDT = "Visual"),
                     difficulty = c(Standard = "Standard", Easy = "Easy", Hard = "Hard")
                   )) +
        scale_color_manual(values = effort_colors) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = c("Mean" = "gray30"), guide = "none") +
        scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, 25)) +
        labs(x = "Effort Condition", y = "Accuracy (%)", color = "Effort") +
        theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
        theme(
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
          panel.border = element_rect(color = "gray70", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5),
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95", color = "gray70"),
          strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
          legend.position = "right",
          panel.spacing = unit(0.8, "lines")
        )
      print(p1)
      # Optional: uncomment to verify figure vs narrative alignment
      # cat("Figure 7 cell means (subject-averaged):\n"); print(fig7_cell_means)
      # cat("Figure 7 marginal by difficulty:\n"); print(fig7_marginal_diff)
    } else {
      cat("Accuracy distribution plot: No data available.\n")
    }
  } else {
    cat("Accuracy distribution plot: Required columns not found.\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("Accuracy distribution plot: Behavioral data not available.\n")
}
```

```{r}
# MOVED TO SUPPLEMENT: Descriptive statistics tables replaced with visualizations per advisor feedback

# Compute RT descriptives
if (!is.null(behavioral_data)) {
  # Standardize RT column name
  if ("rt" %in% names(behavioral_data)) {
    rt_col <- "rt"
  } else if ("resp1RT" %in% names(behavioral_data)) {
    rt_col <- "resp1RT"
  } else if ("RT" %in% names(behavioral_data)) {
    rt_col <- "RT"
  } else {
    rt_col <- NULL
  }
  
  if (!is.null(rt_col) && !is.null(task_col) && !is.null(diff_col) && !is.null(effort_col)) {
    # Get subject ID column
    subj_col <- if ("subject_id" %in% names(behavioral_data)) "subject_id" else if ("sub" %in% names(behavioral_data)) "sub" else NULL
    
    if (!is.null(subj_col)) {
      # Global RT characteristics
      global_rt <- behavioral_data %>%
        filter(!is.na(!!sym(rt_col)), !!sym(rt_col) > 0) %>%
        summarise(
          n_trials = n(),
          mean_rt = round(mean(!!sym(rt_col), na.rm = TRUE), 3),
          sd_rt = round(sd(!!sym(rt_col), na.rm = TRUE), 3),
          median_rt = round(median(!!sym(rt_col), na.rm = TRUE), 3),
          q25_rt = round(quantile(!!sym(rt_col), 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
          q75_rt = round(quantile(!!sym(rt_col), 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
          iqr_rt = round(q75_rt - q25_rt, 3),
          min_rt = round(min(!!sym(rt_col), na.rm = TRUE), 3),
          max_rt = round(max(!!sym(rt_col), na.rm = TRUE), 3)
        )
      
      # Condition-wise RT summary (subject-level medians)
      rt_by_condition <- behavioral_data %>%
        filter(!is.na(!!sym(rt_col)), !!sym(rt_col) > 0) %>%
        group_by(!!sym(task_col), !!sym(diff_col), !!sym(effort_col), !!sym(subj_col)) %>%
        summarise(
          median_rt_subj = median(!!sym(rt_col), na.rm = TRUE),
          mean_rt_subj = mean(!!sym(rt_col), na.rm = TRUE),
          .groups = "drop"
        ) %>%
        group_by(!!sym(task_col), !!sym(diff_col), !!sym(effort_col)) %>%
        summarise(
          mean_rt = round(mean(median_rt_subj, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
          sd_rt = round(sd(median_rt_subj, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
          median_rt = round(median(median_rt_subj, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
          q25_rt = round(quantile(median_rt_subj, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
          q75_rt = round(quantile(median_rt_subj, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
          iqr_rt = round(q75_rt - q25_rt, 3),
          n_subjects = n(),
          .groups = "drop"
        ) %>%
        # Clean up factor labels for display
        mutate(
          Task = case_when(
            !!sym(task_col) == "ADT" ~ "ADT",
            !!sym(task_col) == "VDT" ~ "VDT",
            TRUE ~ as.character(!!sym(task_col))
          ),
          Difficulty = case_when(
            !!sym(diff_col) == "Standard" ~ "Standard",
            !!sym(diff_col) == "Easy" ~ "Easy",
            !!sym(diff_col) == "Hard" ~ "Hard",
            TRUE ~ as.character(!!sym(diff_col))
          ),
          Effort = case_when(
            !!sym(effort_col) == "Low_5_MVC" ~ "Low (5% MVC)",
            !!sym(effort_col) == "High_40_MVC" ~ "High (40% MVC)",
            !!sym(effort_col) == "low" ~ "Low (5% MVC)",
            !!sym(effort_col) == "high" ~ "High (40% MVC)",
            TRUE ~ as.character(!!sym(effort_col))
          )
        )
      
      # Store global_rt for use in summary text
      assign("global_rt", global_rt, envir = .GlobalEnv)
      
      # Display global RT with cleaner formatting
      global_rt %>%
        transmute(
          `N Trials` = n_trials,
          `Mean (s)` = mean_rt,
          `SD (s)` = sd_rt,
          `Median (s)` = median_rt,
          `IQR (s)` = iqr_rt,
          `Min (s)` = min_rt,
          `Max (s)` = max_rt
        ) %>%
        gt() %>%
        fmt_number(columns = where(is.numeric) & !matches("N Trials"), decimals = 3) %>%
        fmt_number(columns = matches("N Trials"), decimals = 0)
    } else {
      cat("**RT Descriptives**:\n")
      cat("Subject ID column not found. Please ensure data contains: subject_id or sub\n")
    }
  } else {
    cat("**RT Descriptives**:\n")
    cat("RT column not identified. Please ensure data contains: rt/resp1RT/RT column\n")
  }
} else {
  # Placeholder
  tibble(
    Metric = c("N Trials", "Mean RT (s)", "SD (s)", "Median RT (s)", "IQR (s)", "Range (s)"),
    Value = c(
      "17,834",
      "To be computed",
      "To be computed",
      "To be computed",
      "To be computed",
      "To be computed"
    )
  ) %>%
    gt()
}
```

```{r}
    mutate(

      ),
```

```{r}
        panel.spacing = unit(1, "lines"),
        plot.margin = margin(15, 20, 15, 15),
        legend.position = "right",
        legend.title = element_text(face = "bold")
      ) +
      scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 3), breaks = seq(0, 3, 0.5), expand = c(0, 0.05)) +
      scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1)))
    rt_plot
  } else {
    ggplot() + 
      annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5, label = "RT distribution plot: No valid RT data.", size = 4) +
      theme_void() +
      labs(title = "RT Distribution by Condition (Data Not Available)")
  }

    theme_void() +
    labs(title = "RT Distribution by Condition (Data Not Available)")
}
```

### A7.4 RT Timing Validation {.unnumbered}

As described in Methods, we adopted probe-onset-locked RT as our primary timing convention. @fig-rt-distributions confirms the expected 0.35-s rightward shift between cue-locked and probe-onset-locked RT distributions, validating correct implementation of the timing transformation. The probe-onset distribution incorporates the fixed post-probe delay (0.35 s) plus the response-window RT component, whereas cue-locked RT reflects only the response-window component. Subsequent DDM analyses use probe-onset-locked RT, with cue-locked RT serving as a sensitivity check (Appendix~A4.2).

```{r}
#| label: fig-rt-distributions
#| fig-cap: "RT Timing Convention Validation. Histograms showing the distribution of response times for cue-locked (measured from response-window onset) and probe-onset-locked (measured from probe stimulus onset) RT definitions across all trials. The probe-onset distribution is shifted rightward by approximately 0.35 s, corresponding to the fixed post-probe delay before the response window opens. This shift validates correct implementation of the timing transformation described in Methods. All primary analyses use probe-onset-locked RT."
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-pos: "htbp"
#| out-width: "70%"
library(ggplot2)
rt_data_file <- file.path("data", "ddm_ready_data_unthresholded.csv")
if (file.exists(rt_data_file)) {
  rt_data <- read_csv(rt_data_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
  rt_cue_col <- if ("rt_cue_locked" %in% names(rt_data)) "rt_cue_locked" else "rt"
  rt_plot_data <- rt_data %>%
    filter(!is.na(!!sym(rt_cue_col)), !is.na(rt_probe_onset_locked)) %>%
    mutate(
      cue_locked = !!sym(rt_cue_col),
      probe_onset_locked = rt_probe_onset_locked
    ) %>%
    select(cue_locked, probe_onset_locked) %>%
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "rt_type", values_to = "rt") %>%
    mutate(
      rt_type = case_when(
        rt_type == "cue_locked" ~ "Cue-locked RT",
        rt_type == "probe_onset_locked" ~ "Probe-onset-locked RT",
        TRUE ~ rt_type
      )
    ) %>%
    filter(rt > 0, rt < 5)
  p_rt_dist <- ggplot(rt_plot_data, aes(x = rt, fill = rt_type)) +
    geom_histogram(alpha = 0.6, bins = 50, position = "identity") +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(
        "Cue-locked RT" = "#6794bb",
        "Probe-onset-locked RT" = "#d35e60"
      )
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~rt_type, ncol = 1) +
    labs(x = "Response Time (s)", y = "Frequency", fill = "RT Definition") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
      axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
  print(p_rt_dist)
} else {
  invisible(NULL)
}
```
